title: DC-area forecast: Turning mainly clear tonight ahead of a mild Saturday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Humidity is falling off as temperatures slide through the 80s and into the 70s around sunset. Trending mainly clear into tonight.

What's next? Mostly sunny and less humid tomorrow, then more humid Sunday as a new warming trend begins. A full-blown heat wave is probable into the next workweek.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: An isolated evening shower or rumble in Southern Maryland aside, it's trending clearer and less humid as lows range across the 60s outside the Beltway to near 70 in DC. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Saturday): Other than high clouds filtering some sunshine, we've got a fairly bright day. Highs still mainly in the mid-80s. Noticeably less humid with dew points not far from 60. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Mainly clear, with lows in the 60s to near 70 again. Patchy fog is possible nearer dawn as humidity is on the rise. Confidence: Medium

Sunday: Highs in the mid-80s to around 90 are the start of a new warming trend. With more humid dew points back near 70, the heat index could touch the mid-90s in a few spots. A very early morning shower is possible, with an isolated late-afternoon storm chance as well. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Sunday night: Partly cloudy and humid. Lows within a few degrees of 70. Confidence: Medium

Increased heat for the workweek, with highs near 90 to mid-90s both Monday and Tuesday. Skies are mainly bright. Monday may squeak by rain-free, but Tuesday could see a couple of showers or storms late. Confidence: Medium

Storm chances rise Wednesday and Thursday, around when the heat wave may peak. Highs as hot as the mid- and upper 90s are possible. We’ll need to watch the timing of the next cold front by Thursday, when highs could be held closer to 90 if it arrives fast enough. Stay tuned.

DC weather history for August 28

Extreme heat in 1948 pushed temperatures to 99 degrees, while later years brought tropical impacts—from tornadoes spawned by Hurricane Andrew’s remnants in 1992 to damaging winds and flooding from Hurricane Irene in 2011.

Today's daily digit — 6/10: A decent, warm day, albeit still fairly humid, with just an isolated rain chance. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day's weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
